cases.expected: the same JsonSchema instance on which findAncestor() is invoked
cases.description: When the schema has no parent (getParentSchema() returns null), findAncestor() should return the current instance.

cases.expected: the top‑most parent JsonSchema instance (the root of the chain)
cases.description: A schema whose getParentSchema() returns another JsonSchema whose own parent is null. findAncestor() must recurse once and return that parent.

cases.expected: the ultimate root JsonSchema instance at the head of the chain
cases.description: A schema with a chain of three or more ancestors (A → B → C → null). findAncestor() should recursively walk the chain and return C, the schema whose parent is null.

cases.expected: StackOverflowError or a safe termination if implementation guards against cycles
cases.description: Create two schemas that reference each other as parents (A.getParentSchema() → B, B.getParentSchema() → A). The current implementation has no cycle detection, so invoking findAncestor() will cause infinite recursion leading to StackOverflowError. This test verifies the current behaviour (i.e., that a StackOverflowError is thrown).

cases.expected: StackOverflowError (due to infinite recursion when a schema's parent is itself)
cases.description: Create a JsonSchema instance whose getParentSchema() returns the same instance. Invoking findAncestor() should recurse without termination and result in a StackOverflowError, confirming that the current implementation lacks cycle detection for self‑references.

cases.expected: the same JsonSchema instance on both calls
cases.description: Obtain a root schema (parent == null). Call findAncestor() twice on the same instance and verify that each call returns the original root object, demonstrating that the method is idempotent for root schemas.

group: Deep non‑cyclic parent chain within safe recursion depth

cases.expected: the top‑most parent JsonSchema instance (the root of the 50‑level chain)
cases.description: Construct a chain of 50 JsonSchema objects where each schema's parent points to the next one, ending with a root whose parent is null. findAncestor() should successfully recurse through all levels and return the root without throwing an error.

group: Deep chain exceeding typical stack depth

cases.expected: StackOverflowError (recursion depth too large for the JVM stack)
cases.description: Create a chain of 2000 JsonSchema objects (or a number that reliably exceeds the default JVM stack limit). Invoking findAncestor() is expected to overflow the stack, confirming that the method relies on recursion and has practical depth limits.

group: Parent schema throws exception on getParentSchema()

cases.description: Define a subclass of JsonSchema that overrides getParentSchema() to throw a RuntimeException. When findAncestor() is called on a child schema whose parent is this faulty instance, the exception should bubble up, verifying that findAncestor() does not swallow unexpected errors from the parent accessor.
